2016 Agreement: The Nurses and Midwives (Victorian Public Sector) (Single Interest Employers) Enterprise Agreement 2016-2020.
2020 Agreement: The Nurses and Midwives (Victorian Public Sector) (Single Interest Employers) Enterprise Agreement 2020-2024.
ADO: Accrued day off, as defined by clause 43.1.
Adoption: Includes the placement of a Child by permanent care order, and includes kinship care where it is comparable to adoption, having regard for all the circumstances.
Allowable Period of Absence: Five weeks in addition to the total period of paid annual, long service or personal leave which the Employee actually receives on termination or for which they are paid in lieu.
AMUM: Associate Midwife Unit Manager — a Registered Midwife who assists in the overall clinical and administrative management of a ward or unit and deputises for the Midwife Unit Manager when required.
ANUM: Associate Nurse Unit Manager — a Registered Nurse who assists in the overall clinical and administrative management of a ward or unit and deputises for the Nurse Unit Manager when required.
Bank Employee: A directly employed casual Employee engaged in relieving work of a casual nature.
Campus: A site operated by an Employer that provides day procedure surgery, multi-day inpatient services, or residential aged care. Excludes community health centres, sites providing only non-High Care aged care beds, Dental Health Services Victoria, and private residences.
Commission: The Fair Work Commission or any successor body.
Deputy DON: An Employee who is a Registered Nurse appointed as the Deputy Director of Nursing, who deputises for the DON and assists in nursing administration.
DOH: Victorian Department of Health or any successor department.
DOM: Director of Midwifery — a Registered Midwife appointed as the senior midwifery executive officer, responsible for the maternity service/division.
DON: Director of Nursing — a Registered Nurse appointed as the principal nursing executive officer, responsible for the nursing service and any other service (including the training of nurses).
Early Parenting Centre: A centre providing help and support for families with children aged 0–3 who have difficulties establishing feeding and early childhood routines. Includes Tweddle Child and Family Health Services, The Queen Elizabeth Centre, and the O'Connell Family Centre.
Employee: A Registered Nurse, Registered Midwife, Enrolled Nurse, Registered Undergraduate Student of Nursing, Registered Undergraduate Student of Midwifery, Registered Enrolled Nurse Student, or Trainee Enrolled Nurse employed by an Employer covered by this Agreement.
Employer: Any of the health sector agencies listed in Appendix 1 of this Agreement.
Enrolled Nurse: A person registered in Division 2 Enrolled Nurses of the Register of Nurses of the NMBA, including certain mothercraft nurses and early parenting practitioners; excludes persons employed solely or predominantly in the provision of Public Mental Health Services.
Experience: Paid service as a registered nurse, registered midwife or enrolled nurse following registration by the professional registration body. Subject to conditions for Internationally Qualified Nurses or Midwives (IQNMs) where conditions, bridging programs or outcome-based assessments apply.
FFPPOOA: First full pay period on or after. Note: this Agreement spells this abbreviation 'FFPPOOA' (not 'FFPPOA' as used in other EBAs).
Hospital Certificate: Does not include an Employee's base qualification.
HSR: Health and safety representative (including a deputy health and safety representative).
Immediate family: A spouse (including former spouse, de facto partner and former de facto partner) of the Employee; and a child (including adopted, step, current foster or ex-nuptial child), parent, grandparent, grandchild or sibling of the Employee or of the Employee's spouse.
Kin: Another person who is related to the first person according to Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander kinship rules.
Level: A role in which the weekly salary in Schedule 2 is at least equal to or comparable to the weekly salary for the position in which the Employee is, or is about to be, employed.
MUM: Midwife Unit Manager — a Registered Midwife in charge of a maternity ward or unit, classified at Nurse Manager grade NM 2, 3 or 4.
NES: National Employment Standards as contained in sections 59 to 131 of the Fair Work Act 2009.
NMBA: Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (including its predecessor bodies).
NUM: Nurse Unit Manager — a Registered Nurse in charge of a ward or unit, classified at Nurse Manager grade NM 2, 3 or 4.
Nurse: A Registered Nurse or Enrolled Nurse.
Pool Employee: A class of non-casual Employees who agree to be available for deployment across all or part of a Health Service.
Public Mental Health Services: Mental health services delivered on a service, department, unit or program level, operated by an employer covered by the Mental Health Services Enterprise Agreement (or its successor).
Registered Health Practitioner: An individual registered under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law to practise a health profession, other than as a student.
Registered Midwife: A person registered as a Midwife on the Register of Midwives of the NMBA established under the Health Practitioners Regulation National Law Act 2009.
Registered Nurse: A person registered in Division 1 Registered Nurses of the Register of Nurses of the NMBA; excludes persons employed solely or predominantly in the provision of Public Mental Health Services.
Relevant qualification: A qualification, certificate or course of study considered relevant based on: (a) the nature of the education and the Employee's current area of practice; and (b) other factors including clinical area of work, classification, position description, and whether the education would assist the Employee in performing their role.
Safe Patient Care Act: Safe Patient Care (Nurse to Patient and Midwife to Patient Ratios) Act 2015 (Vic).
Shiftworker: For NES purposes, an Employee who is regularly rostered over seven days of the week and regularly works on weekends.
Short Shift: A shift of six hours duration in addition to a 30-minute meal break.
24 hours a day, seven days per week area: Wards, units or divisions of a hospital Campus/facility that have a staffing roster operating over 24 hours a day for seven days a week.
Union: ANMF for all Employees, or HSU with respect to Enrolled Nurses only.
VHIA: Victorian Hospitals' Industrial Association — the employers' representative body.
WIC: Workplace Implementation Committee, referenced at clause 80.10.
WIRC Act: Workplace Injury Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2013 (Vic), or where applicable the Accident Compensation Act 1985 (Vic) or the Workers Compensation Act 1958 (Vic).
Year of Experience: An average of three shifts or more per week in a year. An Employee averaging less than three shifts per week (or 48 hours per fortnight, whichever is lesser) must complete an additional year to advance to the next increment.
